verdicts.message: Interpolated log message defeats structured logging: `info` at line 53 is handed a template literal with `${…}` substitutions as its message, so the logger receives one finished string — the values in it cannot be queried, filtered or aggregated as fields, and every occurrence reads as a different message. Pass the values beside a constant message instead: `logger.info({ orderId, status }, 'order status updated')` for pino and bunyan, `logger.info('order status updated', { orderId, status })` for winston. If these calls go through a NestJS `Logger` routed into pino, nestjs-pino forwards an object first argument as fields in the same way.
verdicts.reason: `log` is the import command's ImportLog console sink (it writes a line to stdout for the operator), not a pino logger; the rule matches the receiver name `log`.

verdicts.message: Not all async functions that make a request accept an AbortSignal: Only 2/3 async functions that make a cancellable request (fetch, axios, ky, ofetch) accept an AbortSignal or pass one on, so a request keeps running after whatever wanted it has given up — a page navigated away from, an unmounted component, a timed-out job. Take a `signal` (or an options object that carries one) and hand it to the request; where nothing could ever cancel the call, omitting it is a deliberate choice — judge against how the function is used.
